Also note in the docstring that the returned parcel-averaged value is not itself distributed as a z (measured null sd 0.230 at 20 independent vertices, i.e. ~1/sqrt(n_vertices)), so it must always be tested by permutation — as scripts/detection_floor_table.py correctly already does — and never against 1.96.

findings.title: event_locked_response indexes prediction rows as TR indices, but TribeModel.predict returns kept-segment rows with no row->time map
findings.claim: The function documents `preds: (n_trs, n_vertices)` and computes `rows = onsets_tr + lag_trs` as direct row indices. The only producer of `preds` in this project returns `(n_kept_segments, n_vertices)` — segments with no events are dropped — and the row->time mapping lives in the `all_segments` list that this API neither accepts nor mentions. Nothing checks the assumption, so a misaligned read is silent, which is the project's declared signature bug class.
findings.evidence: tribev2/demo_utils.py predict(): `for t in np.arange(0, segment.duration - 1e-2, self.data.TR): batch_segments.append(segment.copy(offset=t, duration=self.data.TR))`, then `keep = np.array([len(s.ns_events) > 0 for s in batch_segments])`, `y_pred = rearrange(y_pred, "b d t -> (b t) d")[keep]`, returning "preds : np.ndarray Array of shape ``(n_kept_segments, n_vertices)``" plus "all_segments : list Corresponding segment objects aligned with *preds*". ops/interface-contracts.md states it too: "IMPORTANT: n_kept_segments <= n_total_segments because empty segments are removed". The audited code ignores all of this: `rows = np.asarray(list(onsets_tr), dtype=int) + int(lag_trs)` ... `return p[rows][:, verts].mean(axis=1)`, with the only guard being a bounds check.
findings.concrete_failure: D028 mandates "one unique `timeline` per clip" for batched runs and makes the prediction bank the project spine, so a bank read is a concatenation of per-clip row blocks. Block lengths are not constant: the dummy CategoricalEvent spans `timeline.start.min()` to `timeline.stop.max()` (main.py:186-195) and overlap is `mask = (starts < stop) & (stops > start)`, so a 10.000 s clip keeps rows t=0..9 (10 rows) while a 10.040 s clip keeps t=0..10 (11 rows). Gate 0 v3b's own delivered clips are certified at "10.000-10.040 s" (D023(g)/D024(a)), i.e. both lengths are present in the existing stimulus set. A caller who computes global onsets from the stimulus manifest and calls event_locked_response on the concatenated bank therefore reads the wrong row for every clip after the first length mismatch, with no error — a t=+5 read that silently lands on t=+4 or on a neighbouring clip, producing a contrast that is neither the paper's nor anything else.
findings.fix: Either (a) make the API take the segment list: `event_locked_response(preds, segments, verts, onsets_s, lag_s, tr)` and resolve each onset+lag to a row by matching `segment.offset`/start times, raising if the required time is absent from `segments`; or (b) keep the row-index API but require an explicit `row_times` argument (seconds per row) and assert it is contiguous and uniformly spaced before indexing. Minimum acceptable version if neither is done before the deadline: rename the parameter to make the contract unmissable and assert at the call site in S2 that `len(preds) == expected_n_trs` for the single-timeline case, and forbid the function on multi-timeline concatenations.

findings.title: S2's replication ROIs are not the paper's ROI labels, and our EBA proxy contains the paper's PPA parcel
findings.symbol: S2 - The replication (ROI reporting list, line ~394)
findings.claim: S2 is specified as reproducing the published in-silico localizer result and its failure branch is "Not recovered -> we have a bug". But the ROI definitions frozen by the project are not the ones the paper used. The paper names single Glasser parcels; the project uses multi-parcel unions that cross-contaminate the very categories being dissociated.
findings.evidence: arXiv 2605.04326 §5.9, verbatim: "To extract regions of interest, we used the Glasser Multimodal parcellation (40). FFA, EBA, PPA, VWFA, A5, 45, STS, TPJ, MTG respectively correspond to the following ROI labels: FFC, V4t, PH, A5, 45, STSv, PGi, TE1a." (The list is 9 names to 8 labels — VWFA's label is missing — but the A5->A5 and 45->45 anchors fix the alignment of the first three: FFA=FFC, EBA=V4t, PPA=PH.) The project's frozen definitions, D021: "Specificity controls = V1 (low-level) + EBA proxy (right LO2 u LO3 u V4t u FST u PH ...)" and "Positive control = PPA (PHA1-3 u VMV1-3)". So our single EBA proxy contains BOTH of Meta's EBA parcel (V4t) and Meta's PPA parcel (PH), while our PPA (PHA1-3 u VMV1-3) shares no parcel with Meta's PPA at all.
findings.concrete_failure: S2 runs the flashed localizer, reports "EBA" from a 5-parcel union that includes the paper's PPA, and reports "PPA" from a 6-parcel union the paper never used. If bodies>others fails to separate from places>others, the branch rule sends the project to "Stop. Do not run S3. Debug against Meta's protocol" — burning the remaining days of a 9-day runway chasing a pipeline bug that is actually an ROI-definition mismatch. Conversely a spurious place-body crossover could be read as successful replication. Either way the headline sentence "we reproduced the published in-silico localizer" is not supported, because the parcels differ.
findings.fix: Add the §5.9 ROI table to ops/source-of-truth.md as a FROM-DOCS fact (FFA=FFC, EBA=V4t, PPA=PH, A5=A5, 45=45, STS=STSv, TPJ=PGi, MTG=TE1a; VWFA label not stated in the paper — record that gap explicitly rather than guessing left-FFC). In S2, report Meta's exact parcels as the replication-of-record, and report our Gate 0 unions only as a clearly labelled secondary, so the comparison to the published result is like-for-like and the Gate 0 numbers stay interpretable beside it.

findings.title: S2 encodes a 9 s stimulus-onset asynchrony; the paper's methods say 8 s
findings.claim: The plan reads the ambiguous Fig-4 caption ("flashed for 1 second, with an interval of 8 seconds") as 1 s on + 8 s off = 9 s per exemplar, and states this is "Meta's timing". The paper's results and methods text both say "one second every eight seconds", i.e. an 8 s SOA (1 s on, 7 s off).
findings.evidence: arXiv 2605.04326 §2.5: "various categories of images (fig. 4B) are flashed for 1 second every 8 seconds." §5.9: "All images are presented to TRIBE in a randomized order, for one second every eight seconds (transforming them to static videos)." MASTER-PLAN S2: "Flashed-image localizer as silent video: **1 s on / 8 s ISI** (Meta's timing)" and "Cost: 5 categories x 50 x 9 s ~ 2250 s of video ~ 7.2 h ... cut to 3 categories (faces, objects, places) x 50 = 1350 s ~ 4.3 h, or keep 5 categories at 25 exemplars ~ 3.6 h."
findings.concrete_failure: The replication is run at 9 s SOA and the write-up states "we follow Meta's 1 s/8 s for comparability and record the deviation" — a sentence that is itself the deviation, since the paper's SOA is 8 s. Every GPU-cost figure in S2 is inflated by 12.5% (2250 s vs 2000 s for the 5x50 design; 1350 s vs 1200 s for 3x50), which matters on borrowed compute with nine days left. And if the replication comes out weak, the 1 s timing difference in the inter-stimulus recovery window becomes an uncontrolled explanation the project cannot rule out.
findings.fix: Set the SOA to 8 s (1 s image, 7 s blank) in the S2 stimulus builder, recompute the cost table (5x50 = 2000 s; 3x50 = 1200 s; 5x25 = 1000 s), and record in ops/source-of-truth.md that the paper states the timing three times, twice unambiguously as "one second every eight seconds" and once ambiguously in the Fig-4 caption, with the methods text taken as authoritative.

findings.title: No TR parameter anywhere, and onsets_tr / lag_trs silently truncate floats
findings.claim: The published protocol is specified in seconds (t=5 s after onset, 8 s SOA) but the API is specified in TRs, with no `tr` argument to convert between them. TR=1.0 s makes the two numerically identical today, so nothing in the code or tests can catch a unit error. Worse, both the onset array and the lag are coerced with truncating integer casts, so passing seconds — or a correctly converted non-integer lag — fails silently rather than loudly.
findings.evidence: Code: `rows = np.asarray(list(onsets_tr), dtype=int) + int(lag_trs)`. Docstring: "TR is 1.0 s (source-of-truth, verified), so a lag of 5 TRs is 5 s". Executed just now: with a 40-row array where the intended peak sits at row 9, `event_locked_response(p, verts, [8.0], lag_trs=5/2.0)` returns `[0.]` — `int(2.5)` truncates to 2 — and `event_locked_response(p, verts, [8.9], lag_trs=0.9)` returns a value with no error, `8.9` having been truncated to row 8 and `0.9` to 0. Neither call raises. TR itself is a model-config property (`main.py:147: return 1 / self.neuro.frequency`, neuro `frequency: 1` in grids/defaults.py:68), not a constant of the API.
findings.concrete_failure: A future checkpoint, dataset, or the MCP read path with TR != 1.0 s — the whole point of the prediction bank is that strangers re-analyse it — passes onsets in seconds or a converted lag of 5/TR. At TR=2.0 s the intended 5 s peak read becomes a 4 s read, at TR=1.49 s (HCP) it becomes int(3.36)=3 TRs = 4.47 s, and in both cases the function returns numbers rather than an error. The contrast is then off the HRF peak by 1-2 s in an unreported direction, and the result is indistinguishable from a genuine null.
findings.fix: Add an explicit `tr: float` argument (no default, or default 1.0 with the value echoed into any recorded provenance), take `onsets_s` and `lag_s` in seconds, and convert internally with an exactness check — raise if `onset_s / tr` or `lag_s / tr` is not within a small tolerance of an integer, rather than truncating. At minimum, reject non-integral `onsets_tr` / `lag_trs` inputs with a ValueError instead of casting them.

findings.title: The published object is a whole-brain contrast map; the API can only return an ROI scalar
findings.claim: `event_locked_response` averages over vertices unconditionally, so the pair cannot produce the per-vertex contrast map that is the paper's actual deliverable and the basis of its validation against IBC.
findings.evidence: Code: `return p[rows][:, verts].mean(axis=1)` — the vertex axis is collapsed before the value is ever returned, and `event_locked_contrast` then consumes 1-D per-event arrays. The paper's Fig 4 reports "C. Contrast maps obtained from TRIBE's predictions" and "E. Numerical agreement between ground truth and predicted z-scores. Each dot represents one of the 360 parcels from the HCP parcellation (40), and z-scores are averaged for all cortical vertices falling within the parcel." MASTER-PLAN S4 names exactly this as the cheap validation route: "spatial correlation of our in-silico contrast map against **IBC's** real contrast map on NeuroVault — Meta's own validation move, no fMRI download."
findings.concrete_failure: S4's NeuroVault/IBC spatial-correlation check — the cheapest external validation available and the one the model authors themselves used — cannot be run through this API. Producing the 20,484-vertex map requires either 20,484 separate calls with `verts=[v]`, or reimplementing the read outside the audited, tested module, which is where the 07-31 analysis bugs lived.
findings.fix: Give `event_locked_response` a `reduce: bool = True` flag (or add `event_locked_response_map`) returning the `(n_events, n_vertices)` slice unreduced, and let `event_locked_contrast` operate elementwise on arrays so it returns a `(n_vertices,)` contrast map when fed maps. The ROI scalar is then the ROI mean of the map, which is numerically identical to the current path for this linear contrast, so nothing already computed changes.

findings.title: The 'other categories' baseline is a mean-of-category-means the paper never specifies, and empty categories are dropped silently
findings.claim: The docstring presents mean-of-category-means as "the second half of the published protocol". The paper's phrase is ambiguous and, read literally, favours pooling exemplars; the two coincide only for a balanced design. Separately, categories that arrive empty are dropped from the baseline without any warning, silently changing what the contrast is against.
findings.evidence: arXiv 2605.04326 §5.9: "...and substracting the average responses at t=5 for the other categories" — the paper states neither pooling nor per-category averaging. Code: `others = [o for o in others if o.size]` then `return float(tgt.mean() - np.mean([o.mean() for o in others]))`, documented as "each category is averaged first, then those category means are averaged, so a category with more exemplars does not dominate the baseline". Executed just now: `event_locked_contrast([10.0, 10.0], [[], [0.0, 0.0]])` returns `10.0` — the empty category vanishes and only a ValueError for *all* categories empty remains.
findings.concrete_failure: If S2 ships unbalanced categories (the plan already contemplates trading exemplars against categories: "3 categories ... x 50" or "5 categories at 25"), or if attrition removes exemplars unevenly, the reported contrast is not the paper's and the write-up's claim to have implemented the published baseline is unsupported. The silent-drop path is worse: a category whose events all fell outside the prediction window, or that was mis-keyed by name, produces a contrast against a smaller set of categories with no log line, no warning, and no way to notice from the returned float — the exact silent-failure class the project set out to eliminate.
findings.fix: Soften the docstring to say the paper does not disambiguate, state that this implementation averages category means, and note the two are identical for a balanced design. Add an `exemplar_pooled: bool = False` switch so both readings can be reported. Replace the silent filter with a raise (or an explicit warning plus a returned count) when any supplied category is empty, so a missing category is loud.

hostile-reviewer.lane_summary: I read the seven new functions in tribe_tools/roi_stats.py (lines 181-462), the 11 new tests, scripts/compositional_demo.py, scripts/detection_floor_table.py, D025/D026/D027/D029, G020-G024/M001-M006, MASTER-PLAN S1/S2 and §3.1-3.4, ops/source-of-truth.md, ops/interface-contracts.md, the v3b stimulus manifest, and data/algonauts/position_embed_dead.md; I ran the test suite (26 passed, 4.1s) and five small CPU experiments to test specific attack lines. My conclusion as a hostile ICBINB-BIO methods reviewer: I would reject this submission in its current form, and one finding is dispositive. The replacement statistics are not artifact-free — they merely swap a zero-sum artifact for a global-gain artifact, and I reproduced the paper's own "genuine effect detected at p=0.0005" numbers (raw d=+0.0443, ref d=+0.0300, both p=0.0005, glm_z=+2.25) from an 8% condition-dependent multiplicative global gain with ZERO face information injected, while spatial_z — the statistic the paper indicts — correctly returned null on the same data because it is exactly scale-invariant. spatial_z's own docstring states that cancelling global gain was its purpose; the paper removes that control without ever measuring whether global gain is condition-dependent in the real predictions (D025 diagnostic 3 / G020 are still OPEN and the prediction cache is absent from the repo). Separately, the compositionality demonstration's causal premise (FACE clips drive auditory cortex 80% harder) is contradicted by the project's own delivered-stimulus acceptance record (audio RMS p=0.7991, voiced fraction p=0.8953 — matched), 83.2% of its reported goodness-of-fit residual sits on A1, the one ROI carrying the mechanism, and the simulator's run-to-run drift on the headline number (0.048) is ten times the agreement it claims (0.005) because scripts/compositional_demo.py consumes a module-global RNG in both build_brain() and run(). The detection floors are then computed on that same brain at a nuisance parameter fitted to the result they reinterpret. Two further real defects sit in the shipped API: event_locked_response indexes predictions by TR when the pipeline returns kept-segment rows, and event_locked_contrast's event-attribution assumption is falsified by the project's own verified finding that TRIBE's encoder is maskless and bidirectional over a 100 s window. Single missing control that kills the paper: the compositional explanation of the authors' own headline result must be demonstrated on the real 2026-07-31 predictions (is brain_sd condition-dependent? is brain_mean? is Δz_i proportional to z_base,i?), not on a synthetic brain the authors built and fitted. Everything I report is reproduced by code I ran or quoted from the files.

findings.title: The replacement statistics reproduce the paper's own "genuine effect detected" numbers from a global gain with zero face information — spatial_z is the only one immune
findings.claim: The paper indicts spatial_z for manufacturing a confident wrong answer, but the three replacements manufacture an equally confident wrong answer of the opposite sign under a condition-dependent per-clip global gain — the exact nuisance spatial_z's own docstring says it exists to cancel ("This cancels per-clip global gain (a clip that is merely 'louder everywhere')", line 51-52). Whether global gain is condition-dependent in the real TRIBE predictions has never been measured: D025's diagnostic (3) "is g.mean()/g.std() condition-dependent" is still listed OPEN under G020, and the 2026-07-31 HDF5 cache is not in the repo. Additionally, roi_minus_reference's stated guarantee is against an ADDITIVE gain (line 211: "Cancels an additive per-clip global gain"), but the authors' own generative model applies a MULTIPLICATIVE one (compositional_demo.py:83, `g *= 1.0 + rng.normal(0, 0.04)`), which it does not cancel; the shipped test validates only the additive case.
findings.evidence:
I ran the authors' own synthetic brain with ZERO face information and only a condition difference in multiplicative global gain, using the shipped functions:
  gain delta 0.00 | raw d -0.0055 p=0.7656 | ref d -0.0037 p=0.7851 | spatial_z d +0.0026 p=0.3758 | glm_z -0.30
  gain delta 0.08 | raw d +0.0443 p=0.0005 | ref d +0.0300 p=0.0005 | spatial_z d +0.0026 p=0.3758 | glm_z +2.25
  gain delta 0.12 | raw d +0.0692 p=0.0005 | ref d +0.0468 p=0.0005 | spatial_z d +0.0026 p=0.3758 | glm_z +3.46
Compare tests/test_roi_stats.py:176-178, which cites as proof of a GENUINE 0.05 effect: "raw delta +0.0446, p=0.0005 (detected) -> ref delta +0.0463, p=0.0005 (detected)". The false-positive at gain delta 0.08 (+0.0443, p=0.0005) is numerically indistinguishable from the authors' "detected" case. spatial_z returns the identical value (+0.0026) at every gain level — it is exactly scale-invariant, i.e. immune to the nuisance that defeats all three replacements.
Separately, on a clean multiplicative gain: roi_minus_reference no-gain 0.420000, +4% gain 0.436800, shift 0.016800 (34% of the 0.05 effect the paper says it detects); the shipped test's additive +4.0 case gives a residual of 7.8e-16.
findings.concrete_failure: S2 runs the flashed localizer, faces produce a slightly larger whole-brain predicted response than objects/places (a global gain of ~8% — entirely plausible for a higher-saliency category, and unmeasured), and roi_minus_reference reports FFA face-selectivity at p=0.0005. It will also report V1, A1 and any other ROI with a baseline above the reference as face-selective. The paper publishes "the same pipeline recovers FFA/PPA/EBA/VWFA once the published protocol is used" when what it recovered is a global gain. This is the identical failure mode the paper was written to warn about, at higher cost, and the retracted statistic would have caught it.
findings.fix: Before S2: (1) measure the condition-dependence of g.mean() and g.std() on real predictions — this is D025 diagnostic (3), CPU, minutes, and it is currently OPEN; (2) report every ROI's contrast alongside a pre-registered null ROI under the SAME statistic, so a global gain is visible as a uniform shift; (3) correct roi_minus_reference's docstring to state it cancels additive gain only, and add a test with a multiplicative gain that documents the residual; (4) add a gain-invariant statistic (e.g. ROI/reference ratio, or ROI-minus-reference on log responses) or state explicitly that no shipped statistic is invariant to both additive and multiplicative gain and that spatial_z is invariant to the multiplicative one.

findings.title: The compositionality demo's causal premise is contradicted by the project's own delivered-stimulus acceptance record
findings.claim: The entire demonstration rests on FACE clips carrying more auditory drive than NONFACE clips: `a_f = 0.30 + delta_aud`, `a_n = 0.30`, with the fitted delta_aud = 0.24 — an 80% relative increase in auditory-mass drive. The two acoustic quantities that actually drive TRIBE's Wav2Vec-BERT audio extractor were measured on the delivered v3b clips and are matched, with the point estimates running the wrong way. The only evidence offered for the premise is an ASR word count (23.3 vs 19.8, p=0.157), which feeds the LLaMA TEXT extractor, not the audio one, and is itself non-significant.
findings.evidence: From the delivered manifest /home/deveshb/workspace/AI/tribe-bench/notebooks/gate0_v3_stimuli.json, key `acceptance_on_delivered_clips` (the exact clips that produced the 2026-07-31 result): `"audio_rms": {"p": 0.7991}`, `"voiced_fraction": {"p": 0.8953}`. Recomputing per-clip from the verification JSON: voiced FACE 0.4855 vs NONFACE 0.4937 (diff -0.0082, perm p=0.900); audio RMS FACE -35.23 dB vs NONFACE -34.72 dB (diff -0.50, perm p=0.649) — FACE is if anything quieter and less voiced. D023(f) recorded the same reversal on the v2 set and states it verbatim: "The voiced-fraction result refutes the working assumption that FACE clips are dialogue-dense and NONFACE quiet - the measured means run the other way (FACE 0.571, NONFACE 0.674)". Meanwhile compositional_demo.py:19-20 asserts "FACE clips carry 18% more speech (23.3 vs 19.8 words, p=0.157) ... so more speech means more auditory mass means larger spatial sd."
findings.concrete_failure: A reviewer opens the authors' own stimulus manifest, finds audio RMS and voiced fraction certified as matched at p=0.80 and p=0.90 on the delivered clips, and asks where the 80% auditory-drive increase comes from. There is no answer. The demonstration then reads as: the authors postulated a nuisance that their own measurements say is absent, tuned its magnitude until the simulation matched their result, and concluded their result was that nuisance. The retraction is unsupported and the paper's worked example collapses.
findings.fix: Either (a) measure the auditory/STS-pooled FACE-vs-NONFACE response on the real cached predictions and report it as the driver's actual magnitude — this is G021, already specified and still OPEN — or (b) drop the auditory-drive story entirely and demonstrate compositionality with a nuisance that is measurably present in the delivered stimuli (motion is the documented candidate: D023(f) measured it as a real confound and D024(c) explicitly withdrew any claim about its sign through spatial_z). Do not present a fitted nuisance as an explanation of a real result without showing the nuisance exists in that result.

findings.title: The headline agreement ("FFCr sim -0.239 vs obs -0.244, within 0.005") is ten times smaller than the simulator's own run-to-run drift, and the simulator is not reproducible
findings.claim: `RNG = np.random.default_rng(0)` is a module global consumed by BOTH `build_brain()` (20,484 texture draws) and `run()` (the per-clip auditory-drive scatter). Every call to `run()` therefore builds a DIFFERENT synthetic brain and draws from an advanced stream, so `run()` is not a pure function of its arguments. Consequently (a) the d_aud grid search in `main()` compares 25 runs on 25 different brains, so the fitted d_aud=0.24 is partly selected on RNG luck; (b) the per-ROI numbers quoted in the docstring, in tests/test_roi_stats.py:175-178, in D026(3) and in MASTER-PLAN §3.3 depend on call position and cannot be reproduced; (c) detection_floor_table.py's docstring claims "Deterministic (seeded)", which is false for the demo it imports from.
findings.evidence:
Run directly:
  build_brain() called twice in one process -> identical? False; max abs difference between the two synthetic brains: 0.1698
  run(0.24) twice:  FFCr z_d run#1 -0.2612  run#2 -0.2135  drift +0.0477
                    EBA  z_d run#1 -0.3257  run#2 -0.2621  drift +0.0637
The claimed agreement is 0.005 (MASTER-PLAN §3.3 "Ordering exact, FFC within 0.005"; roi_stats.py:36 "FFCr sim -0.239 vs obs -0.244"). The simulator's own drift at fixed d_aud is 0.0477 — 9.5x the claimed agreement.
Separately, decomposing the reported goodness of fit (sum-sq error 0.081, cited in detection_floor_table.py:10 and tests/test_roi_stats.py:172):
  A1   sim +0.020 obs +0.280  sq-err 0.06760  = 83.2% of SSE
  EBA  sim -0.295 obs -0.382  sq-err 0.00757  =  9.3%
  V1   sim -0.124 obs -0.046  sq-err 0.00608  =  7.5%
  FFCr sim -0.239 obs -0.244  sq-err 0.00003  =  0.0%
  total 0.0813
A1 is the ROI that carries the entire causal mechanism (it is the auditory mass being driven), and it accounts for 83% of the misfit — the sim predicts +0.020 where +0.280 was observed, a 14x miss.
findings.concrete_failure: A reviewer clones the repo, runs `python scripts/compositional_demo.py` twice, and gets two different FFCr values, neither equal to -0.239. They then note that the ROI ordering the paper calls "exact" is a direct consequence of the authors setting base[EBA]=0.72 > base[FFCr]=0.62 > base[V1]=0.42 (lines 66-68) — it is an input, not a prediction — while the one number the mechanism actually predicts (A1) is wrong by 14x. The claim "reproduces the observed pattern exactly" is withdrawn, and with it the retraction's evidential basis.
findings.fix: Replace the module-global RNG with a `seed` argument threaded into `build_brain(seed)` and `run(..., seed)` so every call is a pure function of its inputs. Then: report the simulated deltas as a distribution over >=200 seeds with a CI, not a point; report the per-ROI residual table (including A1's 14x miss) rather than a single SSE; and stop quoting "within 0.005". State plainly that the base levels EBA>FFCr>V1 were chosen and that the ordering match is therefore not independent evidence.

findings.title: Detection floors are computed on a synthetic brain at a nuisance parameter fitted to the very result they are used to reinterpret
findings.claim: The paper's third contribution is "a design-requirements table with detection floors". Those floors are generated on the same synthetic brain as the compositionality demo, at `D_AUD = 0.24` — a value obtained by grid-searching to minimise squared error against the 2026-07-31 observation. Every noise scale that sets the floor magnitude is invented and unanchored: 0.05 per-vertex, 0.04 global gain, 0.10 auditory scatter, and baseline levels 0.20/0.42/0.62/0.72/1.00. The floor for raw_roi_mean is essentially the product of two of these invented constants. The script's own caveat concedes the units are unverified, yet MASTER-PLAN §0 ships the table as a headline deliverable.
findings.evidence: detection_floor_table.py:39 `D_AUD = 0.24        # best match to the observed 2026-07-31 pattern`, and line 10: "at the auditory drive difference that best matches the observed 2026-07-31 pattern (0.24, sum-sq error 0.081)". Line 30 imports `build_brain, clip_map` from the demo. Lines 172-175 state: "these floors are computed on a **synthetic** brain whose mass structure is modelled on the printed top-k ROIs, not on the real prediction cache ... the constant relating them to real TRIBE units is unverified until S2 produces real predictions." Arithmetic: the dominant across-clip noise in roi_minus_reference is the 4% multiplicative gain acting on the 0.62-0.20 baseline gap = 0.0168 (verified by direct computation), i.e. the reported floor is set by two hand-chosen constants. The project's own data/algonauts/noise_floor_877771.md states the opposite standard: "That is an empirical detection floor, and it is better than a simulated one."
findings.concrete_failure: The paper prints "detection floor for roi_minus_reference = 0.0XXX raw units" to four decimals. A reader applying it to their own TRIBE run has no way to convert, because raw predicted-response units depend on TRIBE's per-vertex z-scoring of its fMRI targets (noted in D027) and on the model's output scale — neither of which the simulation reproduces. Worse, the floor for spatial_z is the number the paper uses to argue the 2026-07-31 NO-GO was uninterpretable, and it was computed at a nuisance level fitted to that same NO-GO: change D_AUD and the floor changes, so the argument is conditioned on its own conclusion.
findings.fix: Report floors in units of the observed across-clip sd of each statistic (dimensionless, transferable) rather than in synthetic raw units; estimate that sd from real cached predictions the moment any bank exists, and until then label the table "design sensitivity under a stipulated noise model" and put the stipulated constants in the caption. Do not condition the floor table on D_AUD at all — compute floors at D_AUD=0 (pure design sensitivity) and show the D_AUD sweep as a sensitivity analysis. Cite noise_floor_877771.md as the empirical anchor the project already has.

findings.title: event_locked_response indexes predictions by TR, but the pipeline returns kept-segment rows and the mapping is only recoverable from all_segments
findings.claim: The function computes `rows = onsets_tr + lag_trs` and reads `p[rows]`, documenting `preds` as "(n_trs, n_vertices)". TRIBE's `predict()` returns `(preds, all_segments)` where `preds` has one row per KEPT segment; empty segments are dropped by default. Row index therefore equals TR index only when nothing was dropped, and the function has no way to know or check. Its only guard catches a read running off the END of the array — misalignment strictly inside the array is silent, which is precisely the failure class the docstring claims to protect against.
findings.evidence: tribev2 source, demo_utils.py: `if self.remove_empty_segments: keep = np.array([len(s.ns_events) > 0 for s in batch_segments]) ... y_pred = rearrange(y_pred, "b d t -> (b t) d")[keep]` and `all_segments.extend(batch_segments)` — the surviving time information lives only in `all_segments[i].offset`. CLAUDE.md states this as a memorised pitfall: "predict() returns (preds, segments). preds shape is (n_kept_segments, n_vertices), NOT (n_timesteps, 20484). Segments with no events are removed by default." roi_stats.py:262 documents the parameter as "preds: (n_trs, n_vertices)" and lines 271-275 guard only `rows.max() >= p.shape[0]`. The docstring at lines 258-261 claims the guard exists because "a silently clipped read is exactly the class of bug M001 and the 07-28 crash were about" — but the silent read it does not catch is the misaligned one.
findings.concrete_failure: S2 renders the flashed localizer as 9 s per-exemplar silent videos. Any TR whose segment carries no overlapping event is dropped, so a 9 s clip returns 7 rows instead of 9. `event_locked_response(preds, verts, [0], lag_trs=5)` then reads row 5, which is TR 6 or 7, not TR 5 — off the HRF peak, and off by a different amount for every exemplar depending on how its events fell. The face-vs-object contrast is attenuated by an unknown, per-exemplar amount, no error is raised, and the paper concludes "FFA recovered, effect smaller than Meta's" or "not recovered" with no way to tell which.
findings.fix: Change the signature to accept the segment offsets (`segments` or an explicit `tr_index` array from `predict()`), resolve each onset+lag to a row by searching offsets for the matching time, and raise loudly if the requested time is not present in the kept segments. Update ops/interface-contracts.md with the new signature per CLAUDE.md rule 2. As a stopgap, at minimum assert `preds.shape[0] == expected_n_trs` and require the caller to pass that number.

findings.title: event_locked_contrast attributes the t=+5 read to one event, but TRIBE's encoder is verified maskless and bidirectional over a 100 s window
findings.claim: The published protocol the paper adopts presents images at 1 s on / 8 s ISI and reads the prediction at t=+5 s after each image. That read is only attributable to that image if the model's output at time t depends on stimulus near t. The project has independently verified that TRIBE's encoder is non-causal and unmasked over a 100 s window, so the output at any position is a function of every stimulus in the window — roughly 11 exemplars at 9 s spacing. The statistic has no term for this and the API exposes no way to see it.
findings.evidence: /home/deveshb/workspace/AI/tribe-bench/data/algonauts/position_embed_dead.md: "`config.yaml: causal: false`", "`neuraltrain/models/transformer.py:69-72`: `if self.causal: return Decoder(...) else: return Encoder(...)` -> returns the bidirectional `Encoder`", "`tribev2/model.py:233`: `x = self.encoder(x)` — no mask, no `is_causal`", and the conclusion: "Maskless attention means the representation at output position p is a function of all window positions, including everything after p." ops/source-of-truth.md confirms the window: "Dataloader window = duration_trs x TR = **100 s regardless of clip length** | VERIFIED | grids/defaults.py:127-128". roi_stats.py:279-303 computes `mean(target) - mean over categories of mean(category)` with no window or occupancy term.
findings.concrete_failure: With randomized category order (Meta's protocol), each 100 s window mixes ~11 exemplars drawn from all 5 categories, so every t=+5 read is roughly a 1/11-weighted target plus 10/11 mixed-category background. The measured face-vs-other contrast is attenuated by close to an order of magnitude relative to the true per-image response, and the attenuation depends on how the exemplars happened to be packed into windows. The paper then reports a detection floor for event_locked_contrast that is really a floor for a heavily diluted quantity, and if S2 under-recovers FFA relative to Meta the authors have no way to distinguish leakage from a pipeline bug — which is exactly the branch point MASTER-PLAN S2 says determines whether to spend the remaining GPU budget.
findings.fix: Add and report a leakage control: (1) read the ISI baseline (e.g. t=+5 after a blank slot) and report it as a fourth 'category' — it should be flat if attribution holds; (2) run one occupancy sweep (1, 4, 11 exemplars per 100 s window) and report the contrast as a function of density; (3) record and report the window packing (which exemplars shared a window) alongside every contrast. Add the maskless-encoder fact to ops/source-of-truth.md's TR/window block, where a designer will actually see it, and note it in the event_locked_* docstrings.

findings.title: define_froi with its documented default is a no-op on the project's own primary ROI, returning the exact parcel the plan calls wrong
findings.claim: define_froi's stated purpose is to "fix the ROI, not just the statistic", replacing "the raw 58-vertex Glasser right-FFC parcel" with a functionally defined subset. Its default `top_n=100` is capped at the parcel size (`k = min(int(top_n), pv.size)`), so applied to the 58-vertex right-FFC parcel it returns all 58 vertices — the original ROI, unchanged. The deliverable silently does nothing for the case it was written for, and the test suite pins the capping behaviour as correct.
findings.evidence: Run directly: `parcel size 58, default top_n=100 -> fROI size 58; fROI == whole parcel? True`. roi_stats.py:353-357 states the motivation: "Gate 0 used the raw 58-vertex Glasser right-FFC parcel as its face region; a proper functional ROI (fROI) is defined by selectivity measured on data that is NOT the data you then test on (Bladon & Bent use ~104 vertices)." MASTER-PLAN §3.4: "The Glasser/HCP-MMP1 right-FFC parcel reportedly does not show face>object preference even in real human fMRI. Independently: Bladon & Bent use an FFA of 104 vertices; ours was 58. Fix: define the fROI in-silico — run the flashed localizer, take the top-N most face-selective vertices inside the parcel." The arithmetic is inescapable: top-N inside a 58-vertex parcel cannot yield 104 vertices, and at N>=58 it yields the parcel.
findings.concrete_failure: S2 runs `define_froi(loc_a, loc_b, ffc_right_verts)` on the split-half localizer, gets back the identical 58 vertices Gate 0 used, and reports "we defined the fROI from an independent localizer half" in the paper. The stated fix for one of the four mis-specifications in MASTER-PLAN §3.4 was never applied, and a reviewer who checks the parcel size against top_n finds this in one line.
findings.fix: Search a superset region, not the target parcel: candidate vertices should be ventral temporal cortex or FFC united with its neighbours (enough to contain a 104-vertex fROI with room to select), with top_n strictly less than the candidate-set size. Change define_froi to raise (or at minimum warn loudly) when `top_n >= parcel_verts.size`, since in that regime it is not defining an fROI at all. Replace test_define_froi_caps_at_parcel_size, which currently certifies the degenerate case as intended behaviour.

findings.title: The lead contribution is one the project's own record explicitly forbids claiming, and the submission currently contains no real-data result
findings.claim: The paper's stated arc leads with "the compositional statistic inverts real effects". Three separate places in the authors' own record instruct that this must not be presented as a contribution, naming the prior art. The second contribution (detection floors per hypothesis) is conceded to a named incumbent in D029. The third (the worked example) is an unpublished internal result whose prediction cache is not in the repository. The fourth (S2 recovery of FFA/PPA/EBA/VWFA) has not been run. Ten days out, the submission has zero real-data content.
findings.evidence: roi_stats.py:39-41: "This is not a novel finding: it is global signal regression (Murphy et al. 2009, doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2008.09.036) and, for interpretability, arXiv 2512.18792 'The Dead Salmons of AI Interpretability'. Cite, fix, move on." MASTER-PLAN §3.3: "This is NOT a novel methods discovery - do not write it up as one." D027: "**Do not write it up as a novel methods contribution.**" D029 table: "The four-valued verdict / detection-floor-per-item idea | **Veritas**, arXiv 2604.12144 (Apache-2.0): ... per-hypothesis power + SESOI". MASTER-PLAN §0: "The minimum viable paper for 2026-08-29 needs only S1 + S2" with S2 STATUS: not started; G020 status "OPEN — needs the HDF5 prediction cache from the 2026-07-31 Kaggle session", and D028 records that "~4 GPU-hours went missing on 07-31". No .h5, no gate0v2_results.json, and no prediction cache exists anywhere under the repo.
findings.concrete_failure: A reviewer reads the abstract, recognises global signal regression, checks the detection-floor framing against Veritas, and finds the worked example is an internal result that was never published and whose data is unavailable for inspection. Remaining novel content: a replication of the model authors' own published result, not yet run. Reject on novelty and on absence of evidence, with the authors' own repository supplying the citations that defeat them.
findings.fix: Re-order the paper so S2 is the contribution and compositionality is a two-paragraph cited methods note (Murphy 2009; Meloux et al. arXiv 2512.18792), framed as "a known artifact class we walked into, and what it cost" — which is the honest and venue-appropriate framing for ICBINB-BIO. Make the deliverable the design-requirements measurement (n x duration x statistic x ROI-definition -> sensitivity), citing Veritas for the verdict taxonomy rather than claiming it. If S2 cannot run before 2026-08-29, submit the S2-not-yet-run version to a rolling venue (TMLR is already identified in §0 as gate-free and states novelty is not required) rather than a deadline venue with no data.

findings.title: glm_contrast_z is not the estimator it cites, and reports a t-statistic as a z
findings.claim: The function is justified as "What Meta's Fig 4 actually reports", but the project's own reading of Fig 4 defines that quantity as effect/SE ACROSS TIME per vertex within a predicted time series, whereas this function computes effect/SE ACROSS OBSERVATIONS (clips) per vertex — a different estimator with a different null and different degrees of freedom. It then averages per-vertex two-sample t-statistics (computed with ddof=1, na+nb-2 df) over the ROI and calls the mean a z. The mean of N spatially correlated t-statistics has no distributional interpretation, so the returned number cannot be thresholded and is only usable inside a permutation null.
findings.evidence: roi_stats.py:307-309: "Per-vertex effect / standard error across observations, averaged over the ROI. What Meta's Fig 4 actually reports, and non-compositional." MASTER-PLAN §3.1: "A GLM z-score is effect/SE **across time per vertex** — which is not compositional." D027 repeats: "a GLM contrast z (effect/SE across time per vertex — what the paper's Fig 4 reports)". Implementation (lines 337-344) pools variance across observations: `var = ((na-1)*av.var(axis=0, ddof=1) + (nb-1)*bv.var(axis=0, ddof=1)) / (na+nb-2)`. Also, tests/test_roi_stats.py:264-274 (`test_glm_contrast_z_is_unmoved_by_a_distant_region`) perturbs vertices 200: while the ROI is `np.arange(0, 50)` — it perturbs indices the function never reads, so any implementation that does `[:, verts]` passes it; it establishes nothing about non-compositionality.
findings.concrete_failure: The paper reports "glm_contrast_z = 2.25 in right FFC" next to Meta's Fig 4 values and invites the comparison. The two numbers are not the same statistic: Meta's is computed across the time dimension of one predicted series (hundreds of degrees of freedom), ours across 15 clips (28 df). A reader who treats +2.25 as a z and reads off p=0.012 is using the wrong reference distribution, and the ROI-averaged t has no reference distribution at all.
findings.fix: Rename to something that says what it computes (e.g. `across_obs_contrast_t`), state in the docstring that it is a t with na+nb-2 df and that the ROI mean is a summary requiring a permutation null, and either implement the across-time GLM separately if Fig 4 comparability is wanted, or drop the Fig 4 claim. Replace the distant-region test with one that perturbs vertices INSIDE the ROI's brain but outside the ROI in a way that would move spatial_z — e.g. assert glm_contrast_z is unchanged while spatial_z on the same arrays changes sign — so the test actually discriminates.

findings.title: detection_floor reports ~30x more precision than its Monte-Carlo error supports and has no confidence interval
findings.claim: The bisection tolerance defaults to 1e-3 on the effect size, but the power estimate driving the bisection is a binomial proportion over n_sim=200 draws, and because `achieved_power` re-seeds from a fixed `seed` the procedure converges to a floor specific to that one set of draws. The returned number is therefore precise to 0.1% and accurate to roughly 3%, with no interval reported. The table script is worse: it uses n_sim=100 and prints floors to four decimals. Separately, `noise_sd` is in practice estimated from n=15 per group (~13% relative standard error) and propagates approximately linearly into the floor, dominating the Monte-Carlo term.
findings.evidence:
Measured directly, same design (n=15/group, noise_sd=1.0, n_sim=200, n_perm=400, tol=1e-3), varying only `seed`:
  seed 0 -> 1.0830, seed 1 -> 1.1045, seed 2 -> 1.1055, seed 3 -> 1.1045, seed 4 -> 1.1143, seed 5 -> 1.1025
  spread: min 1.0830 max 1.1143, range/mean = 2.8%; requested tolerance 0.0010 = 0.09% of the mean floor.
The estimator is otherwise approximately correct — analytic normal-theory MDE for this design is (z_.975 + z_.80)*sqrt(2/15) = 1.0230, and the measured 1.083-1.114 is consistent with a rank test's asymptotic relative efficiency. detection_floor_table.py:105-129 prints floors as `f"{f:.4f}"` with N_SIM = 100.
findings.concrete_failure: The paper's design-requirements table prints "floor = 0.0231" and a reader treats the fourth digit as meaningful, or two statistics whose floors differ by 2% are reported as ranked when the difference is inside the estimator's own seed-to-seed noise. Since the table's purpose is to tell other researchers which statistic to use, a spurious ranking is the specific harm.
findings.fix: Report the floor as an interval, not a point: bootstrap or repeat over >=20 seeds and print median with range, or raise n_sim to ~2000 and bisect to a tolerance matched to the resulting SE (roughly noise_sd/sqrt(n_sim) scaled by the power-curve slope). Print floors to two significant figures. Add a docstring note that when noise_sd is estimated from n observations, its sampling error (~1/sqrt(2n)) dominates and should be propagated. Also state that the estimator assumes a pure additive location shift with equal variances, which is not the sampling distribution any of the four statistics actually has under the demo's multiplicative-gain generative model.

findings.title: Seven new public functions shipped with no entry in the file CLAUDE.md designates as the single source of truth for all APIs
findings.claim: CLAUDE.md rule 2 is unambiguous: "NEVER change a function signature without updating ops/interface-contracts.md first. The contract file is the single source of truth for all APIs." The 490-line contract file contains no mention of `roi_stats`, nor of any of the seven new functions, nor of the pre-existing ones. The module that the paper will rest on is entirely outside the project's declared API contract, at the moment several of its signatures need to change (event_locked_response must take segment offsets; define_froi must take a superset parcel).
findings.evidence: `grep -n "roi_stats\|spatial_z\|u_statistic\|perm_p\|event_locked\|glm_contrast_z\|roi_minus_reference\|define_froi\|detection_floor\|raw_roi_mean" ops/interface-contracts.md` returns no matches; the file is 490 lines. CLAUDE.md line 55-56 states rule 2 verbatim.
findings.concrete_failure: The two signature changes this review recommends (threading `all_segments` into event_locked_response, and requiring a superset parcel in define_froi) will be made without a contract to update, so nothing forces the notebooks and the S2 analysis code to be checked against them. The project's own history (D009, D022, D023) is a sequence of exactly this: a signature or semantic assumption changed in one place and not propagated, discovered at hour 7 of an unrepeatable GPU run.
findings.fix: Add a `tribe_tools.roi_stats` section to ops/interface-contracts.md listing all twelve public functions with their exact signatures, argument shapes (in particular whether `preds` is TR-indexed or kept-segment-indexed), return types, and raising conditions — before making the signature changes above, as rule 2 requires.

hostile-reviewer.lane_summary: I read the full audited surface (`tribe_tools/roi_stats.py` lines 181-462 plus the rewritten `spatial_z` docstring, the 11 new tests, `scripts/detection_floor_table.py`), the ground-truth documents (`scripts/compositional_demo.py`, D025/D026/D027, G020-G024, M001-M007, MASTER-PLAN S1/S2/S3, `ops/source-of-truth.md`, `ops/interface-contracts.md`, `data/algonauts/position_embed_dead.md` and `lookahead_scope.md`), and Meta's `predict()` in `/home/deveshb/workspace/AI/tribev2-source/tribev2/demo_utils.py`. I ran the test suite (26 passed, 3.9 s), ran `compositional_demo.py` end to end, smoke-ran `detection_floor_table.py` (it does execute; ~1.53 s/experiment), and ran three targeted counter-experiments: (a) the floor table at the confound level it hard-codes (d_aud=0.24) versus no confound (d_aud=0.0); (b) a swap of the two hand-chosen ROI baseline drive constants; (c) seed-sensitivity and exact-vs-Monte-Carlo behaviour of `detection_floor`. The code is clean and the arithmetic is correct — I found no numerical error in any statistic. The paper is nevertheless rejectable on methods, and the reason is uniform: every load-bearing quantitative claim is a property of a synthetic brain whose free parameters were chosen to produce the claim, and the three counter-experiments make that demonstrable rather than rhetorical. Specifically: the three recommended replacements' power curves are bit-identical whether the injected confound is 0.00 or 0.24, so the synthetic brain contains exactly one nuisance channel and it is analytically invisible to all three replacements; `spatial_z` recovers a 0.05 effect at 93% power once that one channel is removed, so its "floor > 0.30" is a measurement of the injected bias, not of its sensitivity; and swapping the two stipulated baseline drive constants for FFCr and EBA exactly swaps the simulated ROI ordering, so "ordering exact" — the demonstration's headline evidence — is a restatement of an unmeasured input. Separately, `event_locked_response` contains a real, shippable bug that will silently corrupt S2: it indexes `preds` rows as if they were absolute TRs, but TRIBE's `predict()` returns only kept segments. Two claims I could not verify and flag as gaps rather than findings: what Meta's Fig 4 actually reports (not in `source-of-truth.md`, no paper text in the repo, no network), and whether Gate 0 loaded TRIBE v2 or v1 (G024 is still OPEN and is a live confound for the paper's "same pipeline" narrative).
hostile-reviewer.search_failures: None. Every command completed cleanly and no search was killed or truncated. All greps were scoped to a single named file or directory with `--include`-equivalent narrowing, and no recursive search was run. Two verification gaps that are NOT search failures and must not be read as null results: (1) I could not verify the docstring claim that `glm_contrast_z` is "what Meta's Fig 4 actually reports" — the claim appears nowhere in `ops/source-of-truth.md`, the arXiv 2605.04326 text is not in the repo, and I have no network access; (2) I could not verify which checkpoint Gate 0 loaded (G024), for the same reason. Both are reported as findings requiring the authors to close them, not as things I searched for and failed to find.

findings.title: The demonstration's headline evidence ("ordering exact") is a restatement of an unmeasured input, not a prediction
findings.claim: The claim quoted in D026 and in the `spatial_z` docstring — that the zero-face simulation reproduces the observed FFCr/EBA/V1 ordering exactly — has zero evidential weight, because the ordering is determined entirely by three baseline drive constants the authors chose by hand and did not measure from anything. Under an sd-shift, Δz ≈ −z·(Δsd/sd), so the ordering of the simulated deltas is forced to follow the ordering of the stipulated baselines. A reviewer will read this as fitting four free parameters (three baselines plus the confound magnitude) to four observed numbers and then reporting the fit as a mechanism.
findings.evidence: `build_brain()` stipulates, with no cited source: `base[idx["V1"]] = 0.42`, `base[idx["FFCr"]] = 0.62`, `base[idx["EBA"]] = 0.72`. I swapped only the FFCr and EBA constants (0.62↔0.72) and re-ran `run(0.24)` unchanged: as shipped, `V1 d=-0.111 (zbase 0.254) FFCr d=-0.217 (zbase 0.815) EBA d=-0.267 (zbase 1.083)`; with the two constants swapped, `V1 d=-0.111 (zbase 0.255) FFCr d=-0.270 (zbase 1.093) EBA d=-0.215 (zbase 0.808)`. The simulated ordering inverts exactly with the stipulated input.
findings.concrete_failure: The paper's worked example asserts a mechanism for the retracted 2026-07-31 NO-GO. A reviewer sets FFCr's baseline drive above EBA's and the simulation now 'reproduces' the opposite ordering with equal fidelity. The mechanistic claim — 'the observed pattern is the sd-shift signature' — therefore survives no falsification test as written, and any conclusion drawn from it about real TRIBE predictions is unsupported.
findings.fix: The baseline spatial z of each ROI is directly measurable and is the demonstration's only real degree of freedom: report `spatial_z(grand-mean map, ROI)` for A1/V1/FFCr/EBA from the actual prediction cache and use those measured values as `build_brain`'s inputs instead of 0.42/0.62/0.72. Then 'ordering exact' becomes a genuine out-of-sample prediction. Until that is done, delete 'ordering exact' from every claim and state that the ordering is an assumed input.

findings.title: The synthetic brain contains exactly one nuisance channel, and it is analytically invisible to all three recommended replacements
findings.claim: `clip_map` scales only the AUD block and explicitly makes the per-clip global gain condition-independent, so the single injected confound cannot touch `raw_roi_mean`, `roi_minus_reference` or `glm_contrast_z` by construction. The comparison that motivates D027 is therefore not a comparison of statistics under a shared perturbation; it is a comparison of one statistic that is exposed to the only confound present against three that are analytically orthogonal to it. This is the definition of a rigged demonstration and it is the first thing a hostile reviewer will look for.
findings.evidence: `clip_map` body: `g[idx["AUD"]] *= 1.0 + aud_drive` (only AUD touched); `g += rng.normal(0, 0.05, N_VERTS)` and `g *= 1.0 + rng.normal(0, 0.04)` with the comment `# per-clip global gain, condition-independent`. I ran the floor computation at two confound levels (N_SIM=30, N_PERM=200, alpha=0.025). Power at effect 0.02 / 0.05 / 0.10 — d_aud=0.24: raw 0.47/1.00/1.00, ref 0.80/1.00/1.00, glm 0.50/1.00/1.00, spatial_z 0.00/0.00/0.10. d_aud=0.00: raw 0.47/1.00/1.00, ref 0.80/1.00/1.00, glm 0.50/1.00/1.00, spatial_z 0.40/0.93/1.00. The three replacement columns are bit-identical across a 0.24 change in the confound; only `spatial_z` moves.
findings.concrete_failure: The paper will claim the replacement statistics are robust where the compositional one fails. The evidence offered establishes only that a confound placed in a region none of the three statistics reads cannot move them. Add the one confound that is at least as plausible in real data — a condition-correlated global gain, i.e. FACE clips being 'louder everywhere' because they carry 18% more speech — and `raw_roi_mean` inherits it in full while `spatial_z` is the statistic that removes it. The recommendation to demote `spatial_z` in favour of `raw_roi_mean` is unsupported by this simulation and may be backwards for that nuisance.
findings.fix: Add at least two more nuisance channels to `clip_map`, each switchable and each condition-correlated: (a) a global additive/multiplicative gain whose magnitude differs between conditions, and (b) non-zero auditory-correlated drive inside the pre-registered reference region. Report the full statistic × nuisance-channel matrix. The paper's recommendation must be conditional on which nuisances are present, and the code should say which nuisance each statistic is and is not robust to.

findings.title: Detection floors are computed at exactly one confound level — the one tuned to reproduce the retracted result — so they measure bias, not sensitivity
findings.claim: `D_AUD = 0.24` is a module constant used by every cell of the table, and it was selected because it best reproduces the 2026-07-31 pattern. Under a one-sided FACE>NONFACE test, `spatial_z` at that confound level is strongly negatively biased, so its 'floor' is a measurement of the injected bias rather than of its detection sensitivity. The table's central comparison is therefore circular for the paper's central claim, and D027's own pre-registered revisit condition cannot be evaluated from it.
findings.evidence: `D_AUD = 0.24        # best match to the observed 2026-07-31 pattern`, used unconditionally inside `one_experiment`. Measured (N_SIM=30, N_PERM=200): at d_aud=0.24 `spatial_z` power is 0.00 at effect 0.05 and 0.10 at effect 0.10, so `interpolate_floor` will report '> 0.30 (never reached)'. At d_aud=0.00 the same statistic reaches 0.93 power at effect 0.05 and 1.00 at 0.10 — an implied floor near 0.03, roughly an order of magnitude below the number the table will print. D027 records the revisit condition 'the floor estimator shows the new statistics are less sensitive than spatial_z on a design where ground truth is known (it should be the reverse)'; with only one confound level in the script, that condition is untestable.
findings.concrete_failure: The paper publishes a design-requirements table stating that `spatial_z` cannot detect an effect below 0.30 while the replacements detect 0.02. A reviewer reruns the same script with `D_AUD = 0.0` and gets `spatial_z` detecting 0.05 at 93% power. The table's headline number is off by ~10× and its qualitative ranking of statistics reverses in the no-confound regime, which is the regime the table is implicitly claimed to describe ('a property of the DESIGN').
findings.fix: Make the confound magnitude an explicit axis of the floor table (at minimum d_aud ∈ {0.00, 0.12, 0.24}) and label every floor with the nuisance regime it was computed in. State plainly in the caption that `spatial_z`'s floor at d_aud>0 is a bias measurement, not a sensitivity measurement, and report its d_aud=0 floor beside it. This also discharges D027's revisit condition, which is currently unevaluated.

findings.title: event_locked_response indexes kept-segment rows as if they were absolute TRs; TRIBE's predict() drops empty segments
findings.claim: The function computes `rows = onsets_tr + lag_trs` and reads `p[rows]`, treating row index as absolute TR index. TRIBE v2's `predict()` returns `(n_kept_segments, n_vertices)` with empty segments discarded, and the mapping from row to time lives in the discarded `all_segments` return value, which this function neither accepts nor consults. The `IndexError` guard fires only when a read runs off the END of the array; it cannot detect misalignment, so a wrong read is silent — precisely the M001/silent-failure class the docstring claims to guard against.
findings.evidence: Code: `rows = np.asarray(list(onsets_tr), dtype=int) + int(lag_trs)` then `return p[rows][:, verts].mean(axis=1)`, with the parameter documented as `preds: (n_trs, n_vertices)`. Meta's `predict()` (/home/deveshb/workspace/AI/tribev2-source/tribev2/demo_utils.py): `keep = np.array([len(s.ns_events) > 0 for s in batch_segments])` … `y_pred = rearrange(y_pred, "b d t -> (b t) d")[keep]`, returning `preds, all_segments`. `ops/source-of-truth.md` marks VERIFIED: 'Dataloader window = duration_trs x TR = 100 s regardless of clip length' and 'A 10 s clip therefore yields ~11 rows of a 100 s window'. CLAUDE.md's memorized shapes state 'n_kept_segments ≠ n_total_segments — empty segments are dropped'.
findings.concrete_failure: S2's planned flashed-image localizer is 1 s on / 8 s ISI. If the events DataFrame carries one video event per 1-s image presentation — the natural way to build a flashed localizer — the ISI seconds contain no events and are dropped, so `preds` has one row per presentation, not one per second. With 50 exemplars and onsets [0, 9, 18, …], `event_locked_response(preds, verts, [0], lag_trs=5)` returns row 5, which is the sixth image's own onset second (true time t=45 s), not the HRF peak of image 1. Every event except the last five is silently misread as a different category's stimulus onset; the last five raise IndexError. The resulting FFA/PPA/EBA/VWFA 'recovery' — the paper's second pillar — would be measured on the wrong timepoints.
findings.fix: Change the signature to take the time base explicitly: `event_locked_response(preds, segments_or_offsets, verts, onsets_s, lag_s=5.0)`. Build a row→offset map from `all_segments`, look up `onset_s + lag_s` in it, and raise loudly if that offset was dropped rather than falling through to positional indexing. Update `ops/interface-contracts.md` per CLAUDE.md rule 2. Add a regression test in which a middle segment is dropped and assert the function raises rather than returning a shifted read.

findings.title: Events sharing a 100 s bidirectional window are not exchangeable, so every per-event permutation null and every detection floor is anti-conservative
findings.claim: `event_locked_contrast` and the `perm_p`/`detection_floor` machinery treat individual events as independent, exchangeable observations. TRIBE v2's encoder is maskless and bidirectional over a 100-TR window, so the prediction at every timepoint is a function of the whole window, including stimuli presented AFTER it. At 1 s on / 8 s ISI, ~11 events share each window and are mutually dependent; furthermore each event's read sits at a different within-window position and therefore has a different amount of future context, which is an uncontrolled covariate of response magnitude.
findings.evidence: This repo's own verified findings: `data/algonauts/position_embed_dead.md` — 'config.yaml: causal:false → neuraltrain/models/transformer.py:69-72 returns Encoder, not Decoder'; 'Maskless attention means the representation at output position p is a function of all window positions, including everything after p'. `data/algonauts/lookahead_scope.md` — 'the prediction for within-window TR p attends over the whole ~100-TR window, including the (99−p) TRs after p'. `ops/source-of-truth.md` VERIFIED: 'Dataloader window = duration_trs x TR = 100 s regardless of clip length'. Neither `event_locked_contrast` nor `detection_floor` has any window or block parameter; `detection_floor`'s model is `rng.normal(effect, noise_sd, n_per_group)` — i.i.d. by construction.
findings.concrete_failure: With m≈11 events per 100 s window and intra-window correlation ρ, the effective sample size is n/(1+(m−1)ρ). At ρ=0.3 the design effect is 4.0, so a permutation p-value computed over 50 nominally independent face exemplars is calibrated as if there were ~12, and `detection_floor(n_per_group=50, …)` understates the true MDE by roughly a factor of 2. A category recovered at p=0.01 could be at p>0.1 under a window-blocked null. If exemplars are presented in category blocks, category is additionally confounded with within-window position and hence with amount of future context, so the contrast is partly a lookahead effect.
findings.fix: Either present one exemplar per forward pass (each event gets its own 100 s window, restoring independence at real GPU cost), or permute at the WINDOW level rather than the event level and report the cluster-robust p. Record the exemplar-to-window assignment and the within-window position of every read, randomize category order across windows and positions, and report response magnitude against within-window position as a diagnostic. Add the window/block structure as an explicit parameter of `detection_floor` and report the design effect.

findings.title: The headline statistic-comparison table is a single unreplicated realization with frozen seeds
findings.claim: The 'THE DECISION-RELEVANT CASE' table — the numbers quoted verbatim in the `spatial_z` docstring, in D026 reasoning point 3, and pinned by `test_spatial_z_inverts_a_real_effect` — is one draw. `clip_map` is called with fixed seeds `1000+i` and `2000+i` in every row of every table, so the per-clip noise realization never changes, and the injected effect is added AFTER the multiplicative gain so it enters noise-free. There is no repetition, no sampling distribution, no Type-I check, and no error bar behind any published number.
findings.evidence: `run()` calls `clip_map(base, idx, a_f, seed=1000 + i)` and `clip_map(base, idx, a_n, seed=2000 + i)` — fixed across all invocations; the effect is applied afterwards as `pf[:, idx["FFCr"]] += face_effect`. My run of the shipped script shows the consequence exactly: FFCr `raw d` is constant at −0.0054/−0.0055 across every row of the d_aud sweep (0.00 through 0.18), and in the effect table it is deterministically `effect − 0.0055`: 0.02→+0.0146, 0.05→+0.0446, 0.10→+0.0946, 0.20→+0.1946, 0.40→+0.3945. The quoted 'p=0.0005' is the estimator floor 1/(2000+1), i.e. zero of 2000 permutations, not a measured value.
findings.concrete_failure: The paper reports 'raw and reference statistics detect a genuine 0.05 effect at p=0.0005 while spatial_z reports p=0.9985'. Whether the null offset is −0.0055 or +0.02 is pure luck of seeds 1000-1014 versus 2000-2014, and it is never resampled. A reviewer reruns with different clip seeds and gets a different table. Worse, because the effect bypasses the per-clip gain, raw's detection is noise-free by construction, so p collapses to the estimator floor for reasons that will not hold in real data.
findings.fix: Wrap the whole comparison in ≥1000 independent replications with resampled clip seeds; report median and 5-95% interval for every cell, plus the empirical Type-I rate at effect 0 for each statistic. Inject the effect BEFORE the global gain so it carries the same nuisance as the signal. Report 'p < 5e-4' rather than 'p = 0.0005' anywhere the Monte-Carlo floor is hit, and state n_perm beside it.

findings.title: The reproduction claim omits the one ROI that carries the posited mechanism, and that ROI accounts for 83% of the fit error
findings.claim: The docstring and D026 both summarize the simulation by quoting FFCr (sim −0.239 vs obs −0.244) and, in D026, EBA and V1 — but silently drop A1. A1 is the ROI the posited mechanism acts on directly: the entire story is that FACE clips drove more auditory mass. The simulation misses A1 by more than an order of magnitude, and that single ROI supplies 83% of the reported sum-of-squares error. The mechanism fails on its own diagnostic.
findings.evidence: Shipped script output at the best-fit setting: `A1 sim d=+0.020 obs d=+0.280`, `V1 −0.124 / −0.046`, `FFCr −0.239 / −0.244`, `EBA −0.295 / −0.382`, total sum-sq error 0.0810. Per-ROI contributions: A1 (0.020−0.280)²=0.0676 (83.2%), EBA 0.00757, V1 0.00608, FFCr 0.000025. The `spatial_z` docstring quotes only 'FFCr sim -0.239 vs obs -0.244, ordering exact'; D026 reasoning point 3 lists FFCr, EBA and V1 and omits A1 entirely.
findings.concrete_failure: A reviewer computes the per-ROI residuals and finds that the single number the paper reports (FFCr) is the best-fitting of four by a factor of 240 in squared error, while the ROI whose behaviour is the causal claim is off by 14×. The natural reading is that the simulation reproduces the three ROIs it was parameterised to reproduce and fails the one that would falsify it, and that the write-up quotes only the former.
findings.fix: Report all four ROIs with residuals and the per-ROI error contribution in the docstring, in D026, and in the paper. State explicitly that the simulation does not reproduce A1's observed +0.280 and explain why (in the simulation the sd rises in step with A1's mean, holding its z flat). Treat A1 as the falsification test the mechanism must pass, not as an omitted row.

findings.title: The two statistics D027 designates as PRIMARY ship with no inference procedure and no detection floor
findings.claim: D027 makes `event_locked_contrast` the primary statistic and adds `glm_contrast_z`, and requires under D-3 that 'every verdict carries a detection floor'. Both return a single scalar with no null distribution, and `detection_floor`'s model — two independent groups of per-observation scalars with additive Gaussian noise — cannot be applied to either. The module therefore ships a doctrine that its own API cannot satisfy for the statistics it promotes.
findings.evidence: `event_locked_contrast` returns `float(tgt.mean() - np.mean([o.mean() for o in others]))` — one scalar, no variance, no p. `glm_contrast_z` returns `float(z.mean())` — one scalar. `detection_floor`'s `achieved_power` is hard-wired to `a = rng.normal(effect, noise_sd, n_per_group); b = rng.normal(0.0, noise_sd, n_per_group); mc_perm_p(a, b, …)`. `scripts/detection_floor_table.py` had to hand-roll a bespoke permutation for `glm_contrast_z` (`pool = np.concatenate([fa, fb]); … glm_contrast_z(pool[perm[:N]], pool[perm[N:]], ffc) >= obs`) because no shipped helper exists, and no floor helper exists for `event_locked_contrast` at all.
findings.concrete_failure: S2 computes `event_locked_contrast` for FFA/PPA/EBA/VWFA and must report a verdict plus a floor for each. There is no shipped way to obtain either a p-value or a floor for that statistic, so the analyst will either invent one ad hoc (unreviewed, unversioned, exactly how `spatial_z` became the primary in the first place) or report a bare effect size — which is the D-3 violation the paper is written to condemn.
findings.fix: Ship `event_locked_perm_p` (permute category labels at the WINDOW level, per the exchangeability finding) and `glm_contrast_perm_p`, promote the hand-rolled permutation out of the script into `roi_stats.py`, and generalise `detection_floor` to take a callable statistic plus a callable data generator so a floor can be produced for any of the four statistics. Add `ops/interface-contracts.md` entries for all of them.

findings.title: glm_contrast_z contradicts the spec in D027 and MASTER-PLAN S1, cites an unverified fact about Meta's Fig 4, and its non-compositionality test cannot fail
findings.claim: Three problems in one function. (1) Both D027 and MASTER-PLAN S1 specify 'effect/SE across time per vertex'; the implementation computes effect/SE across OBSERVATIONS, and `detection_floor_table.py` averages time away entirely before calling it. (2) The docstring asserts 'What Meta's Fig 4 actually reports' — a fact about the model's own paper that is absent from `ops/source-of-truth.md`, which CLAUDE.md rule 1 and M006 both forbid. (3) The test offered as evidence of non-compositionality is a tautology.
findings.evidence: MASTER-PLAN S1: '`glm_contrast_z` (effect/SE across time per vertex — non-compositional, and what Meta's Fig 4 actually reports)'. D027: 'a GLM contrast z (effect/SE across time per vertex — what the paper's Fig 4 reports)'. Implementation: `av, bv = a[:, verts], b[:, verts]; diff = av.mean(axis=0) - bv.mean(axis=0); var = ((na-1)*av.var(axis=0, ddof=1) + (nb-1)*bv.var(axis=0, ddof=1))/(na+nb-2)` with docstring 'across observations'. `detection_floor_table.py` feeds it `fa = np.array([p.mean(axis=0) for p in face])` — time collapsed first. `grep -c roi_stats ops/interface-contracts.md` returns 0. The test: `a2[:, 200:] += 9.0` then `assert abs(before - after) < 1e-9` — but the function only ever reads `a[:, verts]` with `verts = np.arange(0,50)`, so columns 200+ are unread and the assertion holds by array indexing regardless of the statistic's properties.
findings.concrete_failure: The paper claims its GLM z matches the published one. If Meta's Fig 4 is a within-run temporal GLM (effect/SE over TRs with an HRF-convolved regressor, df ≈ n_TRs) and this is a between-clip two-sample z (df = na+nb−2 = 28 at n=15), the two differ in estimator, in degrees of freedom, and in what variance component they treat as noise — a referee who knows Fig 4 rejects on that sentence alone. Meanwhile `test_glm_contrast_z_is_unmoved_by_a_distant_region` would pass unchanged if `glm_contrast_z` were replaced by `lambda a,b,v: 0.0`.
findings.fix: Read arXiv 2605.04326 and record the exact Fig 4 estimator in `ops/source-of-truth.md` with a line citation before any claim of correspondence survives; if it is a temporal GLM, either implement that or amend D027 and MASTER-PLAN S1 to say what was actually built and why. Replace the vacuous test with one that perturbs the ROI's OWN vertices — e.g. a condition-correlated multiplicative gain applied brain-wide including the ROI — and assert the documented behaviour. Add all seven new functions to `ops/interface-contracts.md` (CLAUDE.md rule 2).

findings.title: The demonstration's one falsifiable prediction is untestable because the prediction cache it targets no longer exists
findings.claim: The script prints the normaliser shift under the heading 'THE FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION FOR THE REAL CACHE'. That prediction has never been tested, and the repo's own records say the data required to test it was lost. This is the single missing control that decides whether the paper's worked example is about TRIBE or about a simulation the authors wrote.
findings.evidence: Script output: `brain_mean FACE 0.33924 NONFACE 0.31576 p=0.0005`, `brain_sd FACE 0.40844 NONFACE 0.33370 p=0.0005 ratio 1.2240`. `ops/knowledge-gaps.md` G020: 'Status: OPEN — needs the HDF5 prediction cache from the 2026-07-31 Kaggle session', with the closing tests specified as '(a) test g.mean() and g.std() FACE vs NONFACE; (b) recompute FFC z against a reference mask excluding auditory+STS'. D028: 'Kaggle /kaggle/working is lost on interactive session end unless Persistence was enabled beforehand — which is how ~4 GPU-hours went missing on 07-31.'
findings.concrete_failure: The paper claims the 2026-07-31 NO-GO was a normaliser artifact and offers a synthetic reproduction as proof. The prediction that would confirm it on real data — brain_sd is ~22% larger for FACE clips than NONFACE clips — is stated but never checked, and cannot be checked from any surviving artifact. If the real sd_ratio is 1.02 rather than 1.22, the sd-shift mechanism is 10× too small to produce the observed −0.244 and the paper's central explanation is wrong. As written, the reviewer cannot distinguish 'we proved the artifact' from 'we constructed a simulation that resembles our result'.
findings.fix: This is the single control whose absence should kill the paper: re-run the 30 clips (≈1.5 h T4 per the S2 budget, and the bank is required anyway under D028) and report, on real predictions, (a) g.mean() and g.std() FACE vs NONFACE with the permutation p, (b) FFCr renormalised against a reference excluding auditory+STS, (c) FFCr−EBA per clip. Two of the four numbers are already specified in G020. Without them the synthetic demonstration must be framed as a hypothesis about the retracted result, never as its explanation.

findings.title: G024 is open: the 'confident wrong answer' and the 'same pipeline recovering FFA/PPA/EBA/VWFA' may not be the same model
findings.claim: The paper's structure is 'here is our confident wrong answer, and here is the SAME pipeline recovering the regions once the published protocol is used'. It is not established that the wrong answer came from the same model the replication will use. If Gate 0 loaded TRIBE v1, the comparison confounds a statistic change with a model change, and the in-silico localizer claim being replicated does not exist for the model that produced the null.
findings.evidence: `ops/knowledge-gaps.md` G024: 'the in-silico localizer result exists only for v2 (facebook/tribev2). If any run loaded v1 weights from facebookresearch/algonauts-2025, its interpretation changes entirely. The 07-31 results JSON records the tribev2 commit af58661791a351a448a489042a28f6c37e1c14b7 but the tribe-bench clone FAILED that session and no tribe-bench SHA was recorded. … Status: OPEN.' MASTER-PLAN S2 carries the same warning as a checklist item: '⚠ Confirm which checkpoint Gate 0 actually loaded'. G022: 'TRIBE v1 (arXiv 2507.22229, facebookresearch/algonauts-2025) is a DIFFERENT, earlier model'.
findings.concrete_failure: A referee asks which checkpoint produced the −0.244 and which will produce the recovery. If the answer is v1 then v2, the before/after figure varies two things at once and the paper's causal claim about the statistic is unsupported. G024 is flagged in the repo as 'cheap to close', which makes leaving it open before submission indefensible rather than merely unlucky.
findings.fix: Close G024 before writing: check the `from_pretrained` argument in the Gate 0 notebook and in `tribe_tools/model.py:load_model` against the HF model card, and record the checkpoint revision hash in `ops/source-of-truth.md`. Every figure caption must name the checkpoint. If the two arms used different checkpoints, either re-run the worked example on v2 or reframe the paper so the model change is the stated variable.

findings.title: detection_floor reports a single-seed point estimate with no uncertainty, and simulates a different test than the verdict runs at small n
findings.claim: Three defects in a number destined for a published table. (1) `achieved_power` re-seeds with the same `seed` on every call, so the returned MDE is conditional on one fixed set of n_sim draws and carries no reported uncertainty. (2) It calls `mc_perm_p` unconditionally, whereas the verdict path `perm_p` enumerates exactly when C(N,n) ≤ 20000, i.e. for n_per_group ≤ 8 — so at small n the floor describes a test the verdict does not run, contradicting the docstring's 'the same one-sided permutation test the verdict uses'. (3) The docstring's 'It is a property of the DESIGN … not of any observed data' is false whenever `noise_sd` is estimated from the same clips that produced the verdict, and no estimator is shipped to do it any other way.
findings.evidence: Code: `def achieved_power(effect): rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)` — same seed each call; `if mc_perm_p(a, b, n_perm=n_perm, seed=…)`. `perm_p`: `if comb(N, n) <= 20000: return exact_perm_p(...)`. Measured: `detection_floor(15, noise_sd=1.0, n_sim=60, n_perm=200, tol=0.02)` over seeds 0-4 gives [1.125, 1.094, 1.219, 1.172, 1.125] — a spread of 0.125, 10.9% of the mean. At n=8 with a true effect of 0.9 sd, rejection rate at alpha=0.025 is 0.303 under `exact_perm_p` versus 0.283 under `mc_perm_p(n_perm=400)` (300 replications), a 7% relative power difference; minimum achievable p is 8e-5 exact versus 2.5e-3 Monte-Carlo.
findings.concrete_failure: The paper prints 'MDE = 1.12' in a design-requirements table. Re-running with seed=2 gives 1.22. For a small-n row (n=6 or 8), the tabulated floor is systematically wrong because the verdict would have used exact enumeration with far finer p-value granularity. And an analyst who plugs the observed sample sd of a null result into `noise_sd` gets a floor contaminated by any real effect present in those very data.
findings.fix: Report the MDE as an interval: resample the simulation seed R times and print the median with a 5-95% range, or bootstrap the bisection. Route through `perm_p` rather than `mc_perm_p` so the simulated test matches the verdict's test exactly. Amend the docstring to state that the floor is conditional on the supplied `noise_sd`, and ship an explicit estimator (e.g. from held-out or negative-control clips) so the noise input is not silently taken from the test data.

findings.title: interpolate_floor reports an already-powered design as 'never reached', inverting the conclusion; the script's stated runtime is ~10x optimistic
findings.claim: `interpolate_floor` scans from i=1 for the first index satisfying `powers[i] >= target > powers[i-1]`. If the design is already at or above target power at the smallest effect in the grid (including effect 0.0), no index can satisfy the strict `target > powers[i-1]` clause, the function returns None, and `main` prints '> 0.30 (never reached)' — the exact opposite of the truth. Separately, the module docstring claims '~2-4 minutes' for a script that has never been successfully executed.
findings.evidence: Code: `for i in range(1, len(effects)): if powers[i] >= target > powers[i-1]: …` then `return None`; `main` renders None as `f"> {EFFECTS[-1]:.2f} (never reached)"`.
